# Kaizenly — full site text

Kaizenly is a strict, local-first focus guard for Android, built by Nadeem
Mazhar (Nadeem Dev Apps), a solo developer.

---

## Home

### A little better, every day.

Kaizenly is a strict focus guard for Android. Pick a duration, pick a bag of
distracting apps, and they stay blocked until the session ends. Leaving early
costs parachutes — and there is no easy way out. That strictness is the point.

No download yet — the app is in development.

### Why Kaizenly?

Three words, one habit. Kai is change, Zen is calm, ly is daily.

- Kai — Change. Small change, on purpose. Not an overhaul — one better session than yesterday.
- Zen — Calm. Focus without noise. The phone goes quiet, the apps go away, the mind settles.
- ly — Daily. Every day, not someday. The streak is the product — five minutes a day lays a block.

Kaizenly is Kaizen, daily — the Japanese idea that small, continuous
improvement compounds into something real.

### What it does — Strict where it matters.

Four things, done properly. The full detail — every rule, every limit, every
edge case — is on the Features page.

- Focus sessions — Bags, presets, the wheel, and a block screen that does not let go — with breaks and parachutes for when life interrupts.
- Routines — Three routines that start themselves — on schedule, on the days you choose, each with its own bag.
- The Tower — Five minutes a day lays a block. Seven blocks make a floor. Your streak, built where you can watch it grow.
- Parachutes, earned free — Focus for 30 minutes a day and the streak pays you in parachutes — the first 10 days pay double. Never sold.

### FAQ — Kaizenly, answered.

Q: What is Kaizenly?
A: Kaizenly is a strict focus guard for Android. You pick a duration and a
bag — a named set of distracting apps — and every app in the active bag is
blocked until the session ends. Leaving early costs parachutes, and there is
no easy way out: that strictness is the point. All three bags, all six slots
per bag, routines, and soundscapes are free — and so are sessions up to
12 hours (custom card) and silence during sessions. Everything in the app
is free.

Q: How much does Kaizenly cost?
A: Everything is free to use right now. Bags, routines, soundscapes, and
parachutes are all free — and so are the custom card, sessions up to 12
hours, and silence / Do Not Disturb during sessions. There is no purchase
in the app, and none is planned.

Q: How do I get parachutes?
A: Parachutes are earned, never bought. Focus for at least 30 minutes of
actual focus in a day and that day counts toward your parachute streak. The
first 10 days pay double: day 3 earns +2, and by day 10 you have earned 20.
After day 10 you earn +1 a day, with a +5 bonus at day 20. A missed day resets
the streak to 0 — even if a Tower reserve saves your Tower streak. The full
rule and table are on the Features page.

Q: What happens if I miss a day?
A: Two different streaks, two different rules. The Tower has 3 reserve blocks:
a missed day spends one automatically, and 10 days in a row restores one. The
parachute streak has no reserves — a missed day resets it to 0, even if a
Tower reserve saved the Tower.

Q: What if I open a blocked app during a session?
A: It bounces straight back. The notification shade closes, recents close,
the power menu closes, and floating windows are dismissed. The block comes
back on its own even if the app was closed, and it survives a reboot.

Q: Can I take a break during a session?
A: Yes — a 30-minute break, for 1 parachute, as many times as you need in a
session. The clock freezes while you are on break and the block returns when
the break ends. During a break, enforcement, the overlay, Do Not Disturb, and
sound are all off.

Q: Does Kaizenly store my data anywhere?
A: No. Kaizenly is local-first: sessions live in a local database on your
device, and bags, routines, and settings live in on-device preferences. There
is no Kaizenly account, no sign-up, and no server that receives your data.
The app opts out of automatic cloud backup, so a fresh install starts empty
and uninstalling wipes its local data. You can export and import a local JSON
backup yourself.

Q: Which apps stay open during a session?
A: The essentials stay open: messaging, the dialer, the camera, the alarm,
the keyboard, and in-call screens. Everything in the active bag is blocked —
everything else is yours.

Q: What is the Tower?
A: The Tower is your streak, built. Five minutes of focus a day lays one
block; seven blocks make a floor. Three reserve blocks sit beside it and are
spent automatically on missed days, and ten days in a row restores one spent
reserve. Reach day one hundred and you will find a surprise.

Q: Can I use Kaizenly in the dark?
A: Yes. Kaizenly has Light, Automatic, and Dark themes. A fresh install starts
in Light, and the toggle is in Settings. The dark theme is the design anchor —
deep green-black surfaces with the vivid green accent.

### Your focus belongs to you.

Kaizenly has no account, no sign-up, and no server. Your sessions live in a
local database on your device; your bags, routines, and settings live in
on-device preferences. The app opts out of automatic cloud backup — a fresh
install starts empty, and uninstalling wipes its local data. Your focus data
is yours, and it stays where it was made.

No account. No sign-up. No server. No trackers. Local backup, yours to keep.

### Built by Nadeem.

Kaizenly is built by Nadeem Mazhar, a solo developer, as Nadeem Dev Apps. It
started as his own problem — a phone that would not stay down — and it is
built the way he builds everything: local-first, strict where it matters, and
honest about what it does.

More from Nadeem Dev Apps: https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/my-web/

---

## Features

### Everything Kaizenly does, in detail.

Every feature, every rule, every limit — written down so nothing is left to
guess.

### Focus — One session. No way out.

Pick a bag, pick a time, slide to start. From that moment the apps in the bag
are blocked — and leaving early costs parachutes.

Three bags, six slots each: a bag is a named set of distracting apps. You get
three bags with six slots each, all free. The active bag is the one that gets
blocked — switch bags any time you are not in a session.

The app picker: tap a slot to open the picker — search your installed apps,
see them with their real icons, and pick up to six per bag. Save, and the bag
is ready. A slot can be cleared the same way, any time.

The floating pill: a small pill floats over everything while a session runs —
time left and parachutes at a glance. Tap it to open the app. It never gets in
the way of the essentials.

Presets — and the wheel: start in one tap with 15 minutes, 45 minutes, or 3
hours. Or spin the wheel: up to three of your own presets, from 1 to 720
minutes. Sessions over 3 hours need at least one parachute on board — and
the wheel runs all the way to 720 minutes, free for everyone. The Custom
card is free: it sets the wheel to 12 hours (720 minutes) and lets it run
from 3 to 12 hours.
Tapping a preset animates the wheel to the new value — one tick per minute
crossed.

Slide to start: the slide is deliberate on purpose — the handle has to travel
most of the way before the session starts, so a stray touch never locks your
phone. If the app cannot block yet, the slide opens the setup instead of
starting.

Hold to extend: hold for three seconds and the session grows by 15 minutes —
up to +60 minutes per session. Extending needs a parachute on board (it is not
consumed). A short tap only shows a HOLD hint and does nothing.

Routine-aware sessions: a session that would end inside a routine window
stretches to the end of that window instead — when a routine is enabled and
you have a parachute. One focus, no gaps. The stretch is capped at 12 hours
from now.

Leaving early: slide to exit and the handle answers honestly — with no
parachutes it is dimmed and shakes. With more than 30 minutes left, the slide
opens a choice — a 30-minute break for 1 parachute, or end the session for
1 + 1 per hour left (minimum 2). Tapping outside the sheet, or “Keep going”,
keeps the session running. With 30 minutes or less left, the slide ends the
session directly for 1 parachute.

The block screen: while a session runs, the block screen is the only thing
between you and the apps. It shows the countdown, the end time, and your
parachutes — and after three seconds of idle it rests, dimming to a quiet
clock. Any touch brings it back.

- Essentials stay open — messaging, dialer, camera, alarm, keyboard, in-call.
- The block holds — the notification shade, recents, and the power menu close; floating windows are dismissed; the block comes back on its own even if the app was closed, and it survives a reboot.
- Settings passes — if the protection ever drops, Kaizenly lets you open your phone's settings to switch it back on: up to 3 × 60-second passes per session.
- Always in view — an ongoing notification shows the time remaining and opens the app on tap; empty slots on the block screen open the app picker.

Parachutes: emergency exits that end a block early. A break costs 1; exiting
early costs 1 + 1 per hour left (minimum 2). Earned free by focusing — never
bought.

The 30-minute break: one parachute buys a 30-minute break, as many times as
you need in a session. The clock freezes; the block returns when the break
ends. Enforcement, sound, and Do Not Disturb rest during the break. A break
that would run past a routine's end stops the session there instead — a
routine window is fixed.

Soundscapes: Rain, Waves, White Noise, and City — four sounds generated live
on your device, never streamed, never auto-played. They fade in and out with
the session. All four are free.

Block screen, done right: the countdown, the end time, your parachutes — and a
celebration when you finish. DONE in white tiles, SOS in green when you
bailed. The celebration shows your minutes for the session and for today, plus
the week — Monday first. Share the card as a PNG; the done pill is the only
way out.

Boot restore: restart the phone mid-session and the block comes back. A session
ends when the timer ends — not when the phone does.

Sessions under 5 seconds: a session shorter than five seconds is not recorded
anywhere — no stats, no streak, no Tower block. Everything else counts, and
break minutes never count toward your focus time.

### Routines & streaks — Set it once. Focus on schedule.

Up to three routines — a bag, a time window, days of the week — and Kaizenly
starts the block for you. Routines are free, including each routine using its
own bag.

Routines that start themselves: a routine needs at least one parachute to
enable — the safety net for an automatic block. Overlapping routines ask
before they both fire, and each routine can use its own bag: the bag in hand
is restored when the routine session ends.

The daily streak: one minute a day keeps the streak alive — five minutes on
your very first day. Weeks run Monday to Sunday, and a gentle evening reminder
at 8:30 PM nudges you if today has less than five minutes of focus: “Five
minutes of session lay today's block.”

Built like the app — knobs, not fields: each routine has a name (rename it —
up to 10 characters), a start time and an end time set with rotating knobs, and
seven day faders for the days it runs. A routine's window can be anywhere from
5 to 720 minutes long. Turning all seven days off switches the routine off.

Switching a routine on: three checks, in order — at least one parachute on
board, no unresolved overlap with another routine, and the system permission
the app needs to start on time. If two routines overlap, Kaizenly asks —
“Turn on anyway” or “Not now” — instead of guessing. Switching a routine off
is always allowed, no questions asked.

On schedule, every time: a routine starts itself on its chosen days, and a
reminder arrives 5 minutes before it starts. Change a routine and its schedule
updates within moments. While you are on a break, the Routines tab shows the
break countdown in the header, so you always know when the block returns.

### The Tower — Your streak, built.

Five minutes of focus a day lays one block. Seven blocks make a floor. The
Tower grows as you do.

Life happens: three reserve blocks sit beside the Tower and are spent
automatically on missed days. Ten days in a row restores one spent reserve, up
to three. And if you reach day one hundred, you will find a surprise.

Two counters, not one: the Tower and the daily streak are different counters.
The streak stays alive with one minute a day (five on your very first day); a
Tower block needs five minutes. A missed day spends a reserve block for the
Tower — the repair happens automatically, while reserves remain.

Every block tells its day: long-press any block to see its day — the date, how
many sessions ran and for how many minutes — or “Repaired day · the tower held
up” for a day a reserve saved. The first block carries a note of its own: this
is where it all began. When the Tower is taller than a week, a scrubber on the
right edge scrolls it.

Your numbers, at the foot of the Tower: the Tower screen keeps four numbers —
your best day (tap it to jump to that floor), your total focus time, your
average minutes per day, and your tallest Tower. The streak count lives in the
header badge — tap it any time to open the Tower.

### How to get parachutes — Earn them. Never buy them.

Parachutes are the emergency exits of Kaizenly — and they are earned by
focusing, never sold.

The rule, in full: a qualifying day is a day with at least one session of 30
minutes of actual focus. One qualifying day counts per calendar day, and the
counter is the number of qualifying days in a row.

The first 10 days pay double — because building a habit is the hardest part,
so the start pays more. Day 3 earns +2, and every day after that earns +2
until day 10, which pays +6 with its bonus. After day 10, each day earns +1,
with a +5 bonus at day 20.

A missed day resets the streak to 0. Tower reserve blocks do not save it —
the parachute streak has no reserves. The counter is capped at 99.

Reward table:

- Day 3 — +2 — total 2
- Day 6 — +2 / day — total 8
- Day 10 — +6, bonus day — total 20
- Day 15 — +1 / day — total 25
- Day 20 — +6, bonus day — total 35
- Day 30 — +1 / day — total 45

What an early exit costs: the cost grows with the time thrown away — 31–60
minutes left costs 2 parachutes, 61–120 minutes costs 3, 3 hours costs 4, 4
hours costs 5. With 30 minutes or less left, sliding to exit ends the session
directly for 1 parachute.

Parachutes are spent on breaks (1 per 30-minute break) and on exiting early
(1 + 1 per hour left, minimum 2). Holding to extend and starting a session
over 3 hours need one on board — but do not consume it. Enabling a routine
needs one too.

Where the count lives: your parachutes show in three places — the header pill
(it pulses gently while you have any), the Bag tab, and the block screen. The
buy tiles on the Bag tab open a “Totally free” sheet instead of a purchase —
parachutes are never sold. The app's Profile sheet has a “How to get
parachutes” row that opens the full explainer, with a copy button that copies
it as plain text.

### Sounds — Four sounds, made on your device.

No streaming, no downloads, no account. The sounds are generated live on your
phone, and all four are free.

- Rain — Steady rain, made live on your device. Pick it on the block screen and it starts — stop it the same way.
- Waves — Ocean waves, made live on your device. Nothing is streamed, so it works with the phone offline.
- White Noise — Even white noise, made live on your device. It fades in with the session and out when it ends.
- City — City ambience, made live on your device. The sound stops when the session ends — it never plays on its own.

Nothing auto-plays: a sound starts only when you pick it, and the session
fades it in and out for you.

### Stats — Proof, not promises.

Day, month, and year — every session you finished, in one place. Sessions
under five seconds are not recorded; the rest is all yours.

Three views, one history: Day, Month, and Year — Month is the default view.
Step back through past days, months, and years with the chevrons or the rotary
wheel; you can only browse into the past, never into the future. The readout
under the chart always says the period and the total minutes.

What counts, and what does not: a finished session counts its actual focus
minutes — break minutes are excluded, and sessions shorter than five seconds
are not recorded at all. Bars for days ahead are dimmed; the selected bar is
highlighted in green.

The Tower keeps the rest: best day, total time, average minutes per day, and
your tallest Tower live on the Tower screen — the stats page is for the
calendar, the Tower is for the streak.

### Widgets — Focus, from the home screen.

Two widgets, no app-opening required. Start a session or check the streak
right from where your phone already is.

Preset widget: up to three of your presets, 1–720 minutes. Tap a preset to
open the app with that timer; the play button starts a session straight away.
While a session runs, the widget becomes a countdown with the time remaining.
Add or edit presets in the wheel editor — up to three, from 1 to 720 minutes.

Streak widget: the last 28 days, 4 week rows. Twenty-eight days on the home
screen, today ringed. After 8 PM, if today is still empty, the widget pulses
gently — a quiet nudge, not an alarm. Tap it to open the Tower.

### Settings — Yours, the way you like it.

A small settings page, and every switch does exactly what it says.

Theme: three cards — Light, Automatic, Dark. Dark is the design anchor: deep
green-black surfaces with the vivid green accent. A fresh install starts in
Light.

Haptics: one global switch. Turn it off and every vibration in the app stops —
turn it on and you feel it immediately.

Streak reminders: one evening nudge at 8:30 PM, only if today has less than
five minutes of focus and no session has run. Switch it off and the evening
stays quiet.

Each routine, its own bag: free. Each routine uses its own bag — routine 1
uses bag 1, and so on — and the bag in hand is restored when the routine
session ends. The same switch lives in Settings.

Silence during sessions: free. Do Not Disturb while you focus. It needs the
system permission for it — the app explains why, opens the right settings
page, and switches on as soon as access is granted. If access is ever revoked,
the switch resets itself.

Info: one card at the foot of Settings opens Info — the developer, the
credits, and the app version.

### Backup & privacy — Your data, yours to keep.

Kaizenly has no account, no sign-up, and no server. Your data lives on your
device — and the only way it leaves is a backup file you make yourself.

Local backup: export a timestamped JSON backup and import it back with a
confirm step. It is validated before it is written, and a live session is
never carried over. No drive, no password, no upload.

What a backup carries: sessions, bags and all their slots, all three routines,
your streak and Tower progress, your parachutes and their streak, and your
settings. An active session's timer state is not carried over — a backup never
restores a session in progress.

Protected, even in a file: your parachute balance is protected inside the
backup — editing the file cannot add parachutes — a tampered balance imports
as 0, while your sessions, bags, routines, and settings still import normally.

Nothing leaves on its own: the app opts out of automatic cloud backup, so a
fresh install starts empty and uninstalling wipes its local data. There is no
analytics, no advertising, and no tracking — and no third-party code that
sends data anywhere.

Permissions, only for blocking: blocking needs sensitive permissions — the ones
that let the app see which app is open, draw over the screen, and lock the
device. They are used only for blocking, and only while you have a session or
routine running. You grant each one yourself, and you can revoke any of them
any time in your phone's settings; blocking may stop working, including
sessions already in progress.

No account, ever: there is no sign-in and no profile to create. The Profile
sheet has settings, sharing, the tour, and the parachute explainer — but no
account, because there is nothing to sign in to.

### Everything free — Everything is free.

Free:

- All 3 bags with 6 slots each
- 3 routines — each routine its own bag
- All 4 soundscapes — Rain, Waves, White Noise, City
- Parachutes earned free by the streak
- The Tower, stats, widgets, and local backup
- Sessions up to 12 hours — the custom card, 3 to 12 hours
- Silence during sessions — Do Not Disturb while you focus

There is no purchase in the app, and none is planned.

### First run — Six steps, then focus.

The first run is a short tour, not a form: six steps with square step numbers
and a draggable lever. It explains the block, the bags, and the permissions
the app needs — and you grant each one yourself. Finished the tour and want
it again? The Profile sheet has “Take the tour again”.

### Honest boundaries — What Kaizenly does not do.

- No account, no server — No sign-up, no login, no developer server. There is nowhere for your data to go — and no one to send it to.
- No analytics, no ads, no trackers — Nothing in the app watches you, and nothing is sold to advertisers. Your focus data is yours.
- No cloud backup — Your data never leaves the phone unless you export a backup file yourself. There is no sync and no cloud copy.
- No selling parachutes — Parachutes are earned by focusing, never bought. The buy tiles open a “Totally free” sheet — that is the whole point.
- No purchases — There is nothing to buy in the app — no purchase, no subscription, nothing to unlock — and everything listed as free is actually free.
- No magic — Kaizenly adds friction at the exact moment you would otherwise scroll. It cannot want focus for you — it can only make leaving cost something.

## About

### Built for a phone that would not stay down.

Kaizenly started as one developer's own problem. It was built first for
itself, after trying a lot of focus apps and never finding one that was both
strict and private. Most of them did one thing well — a timer, or a blocker —
but they asked for a login, pulled data to a server, or wrapped everything in
ads and pressure. Kaizenly is a guard that holds the line, with everything
staying on the device. There is no backend and no server: Kaizenly is
local-first by design — no account, no sign-up, no analytics, no ads. Sessions,
bags, routines, and settings live on the phone, and the only backup is a file
exported by the user.

Everything is free — sounds, bags, routines, and parachutes, and so are the
custom card, sessions up to 12 hours, and silence during sessions. The app is
still in development: there is no download yet, and one will appear only when
it is real.

### Why the name — Kaizen, daily.

Kaizenly is Kaizen, daily — the Japanese idea that small, continuous
improvement compounds into something real. Three words, one habit.

- Kai — Change. Small change, on purpose. Not an overhaul — one better session than yesterday.
- Zen — Calm. Focus without noise. The phone goes quiet, the apps go away, the mind settles.
- ly — Daily. Every day, not someday. The streak is the product — five minutes a day lays a block.

### The philosophy — Strict about the session, gentle about the person.

Kaizenly does not believe in pressure, perfectionism, or guilt-driven
productivity. It believes in gentle progress, personal space, and realistic
systems — calm focus instead of chaotic hustle. The session is strict; the
person is not punished for being human.

- Strict about the session — Once a session starts, the block does not let go. Leaving early costs a parachute — that is the deal, and the app says so up front.
- Small steps, every day — Five minutes a day lays a block; seven blocks make a floor. You do not need a perfect day — you need one focused session.
- No guilt, no pressure — The app never shames you for a missed day. Progress is quiet and daily — not perfectionism, not pressure.

### Built by Nadeem.

Kaizenly is built by Nadeem Mazhar, a solo developer — Nadeem Dev Apps. He
plans, directs, and reviews; AI tools do the heavy lifting. Every app starts
as his own problem: Kaizenly began with a phone that would not stay down,
Tsumly with a ledger that never added up.

Questions, feedback, or just want to say hi? Reach him at
nadeem.devapps@gmail.com, or find his work on GitHub at
github.com/nadeemdevapps — his only social link.

More from Nadeem Dev Apps: https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/my-web/

## Privacy Policy

Kaizenly is a strict focus guard, and a private one. This policy explains
what it collects — almost nothing — and where your data lives.

### What Kaizenly collects

Almost nothing. Kaizenly stores your sessions in a local database on your
device, and bags, routines, and settings in on-device preferences. It does not
collect your name, email, contacts, location, or the contents of your apps.
There is no Kaizenly account and no sign-up.

### Blocked-app information

Kaizenly keeps a local list of the apps you choose to block, and records when
they are blocked. That information stays on your device; it is never sent
anywhere. Android's usage-access and accessibility permissions are used only
to detect and block apps during a session.

### What stays on your device

Everything. Sessions, bags, routines, settings, your streak and Tower
progress, and your parachutes are all stored locally. On Android the app opts
out of automatic cloud backup (allowBackup=false), so a fresh install starts
empty and uninstalling the app wipes its local data. There is no analytics, no
advertising, no tracking, and no third-party code that sends data anywhere.

### Backup

You can export a JSON backup of your data yourself, and import it back.
Kaizenly does not upload your data anywhere, and it does not store any backup
on a server. Your backup file is yours — keep it safe, since anyone with the
file can read what is in it.

### Purchases

There are no premium purchases in Kaizenly. The app has no purchases of any kind, so no payment information is ever collected or handled.

### Permissions

Kaizenly needs usage access, the accessibility service, device admin, and the
overlay permission to block apps. Those permissions are used only for
blocking, and only while you have a session or routine running. You can revoke
them at any time in your phone's settings; blocking may stop working,
including sessions already in progress.

### Children

Kaizenly does not collect any personal data, and no data is shared with third
parties. The app has no ads, no account, and no in-app communication with
other people.

### Changes to this policy

This policy may be updated from time to time. The version on this page is
always the current one.

### Contact

Questions about this policy? Email nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.

## Terms of Use

Kaizenly is a strict focus guard, provided as-is. Its strictness is the point.

### Acceptance

By installing and using Kaizenly, you agree to these terms. If you do not
agree with any part of them, please do not use the app.

### What Kaizenly does

Kaizenly blocks distracting apps behind a timed focus session. You pick a
duration and a bag — a named set of apps — and every app in the active bag is
blocked until the session ends. Sessions are designed to be hard to break:
leaving early costs a parachute, and a 30-minute break is available during
longer sessions.

### Local-first, no Kaizenly account

Kaizenly stores your sessions in a local database on your device, and bags,
routines, and settings in on-device preferences. There is no Kaizenly account
and no sign-up, and Kaizenly operates no server that receives your data. On
Android the app opts out of automatic cloud backup (allowBackup=false), so a
fresh install starts empty and uninstalling the app wipes its local data.

### Permissions

Blocking needs sensitive permissions: usage access, the accessibility service,
device admin, and the overlay permission. You grant each of them yourself, and
you can revoke them at any time in your phone's settings. Revoking them may
stop blocking from working, including sessions already in progress.

### Purchases

There are no premium features in Kaizenly. Everything the app does is free, and there is nothing to buy in the app — no purchase, no subscription.

### Acceptable use

Use Kaizenly for lawful personal focus tracking only. You may not use the app
to record, conceal, or facilitate anything illegal.

### Provided as-is

Kaizenly is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any
kind, express or implied, including any implied warranty of fitness for a
particular purpose. To the extent permitted by law, the developer is not
liable for any loss or damage arising from your use of the app, including a
missed block or a lost streak.

### Stopping use

You can stop using Kaizenly at any time. Uninstalling the app deletes its
local data from the device. If device admin is enabled, turn it off in the app
first, or remove it from your phone's device admin settings before
uninstalling.

### Changes to these terms

These terms may be updated from time to time. The version on this page is
always the current one.
